question: I would like to reiterate the concerns set out in question E-001437/20231 and others regarding the Natura 2000 network in Galicia. The Galician and Spanish Governments are failing to ensure the Habitats Directive and the Birds Directive are consistently applied with regard to the Natura 2000 network. It is particularly apparent in how specific protection and management plans are drawn up for each site.

The network also requires urgent expansion, but that expansion is seriously affected by devastating, high-impact plans and projects in Galicia (eucalyptus industry, mega-mining, enormous wind farms, etc.) Given the seriousness of the situation, I would like to emphasise how important it is for protection of the biodiversity areas in question to be upheld, and that protection should be expanded. 1.
Can the Commission say whether Galicia’s Natura 2000 Network master plan and its zoning comply with the conservation objectives set out in Article 6 of the Habitats Directive?
Is the Commission area of the steps the Galician Government has taken to comply with the conservation requirements for these unique areas?
What is the current state of play of the horizontal infringement procedure against Spain initiated in 2003 and how is the Commission following up on the procedure in relation to Galicia?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.11.

2025) As the Commission stated in its reply to written questions E-003312/2025, E-003313/2025 and E-003315/2025 and as mentioned by the Honourable Member, the Commission is handling an infringement procedure against Spain1 on account of the incomplete designation of sites of Community importance (SCIs) as special areas of conservation (SACs) and the establishment of specific conservation objectives and measures for SACs.
The Commission recalls that the horizontal infringement procedure against Spain concerns several Autonomous Communities and Cities. Galicia has completed the designation process for all its 59 SCIs.

However, following an analysis of Decree 37/2014 of 27 March 2014, declaring the SCIs of Galicia as SACs and approving the Galician Natura 2000 network master plan, the Commission considers that Galicia has not set adequate site-specific conservation objectives and conservation measures in all its SACs.

Spain has provided updates on the designation of SACs (in the regions where the process is not finished) and, in 2024, has adopted new guidelines for the Natura 2000 network in which general conditions are defined to set site-specific conservation objectives and measures in Natura 2000 sites. The Commission is assessing the information provided by Spain prior to deciding the most appropriate way forward.
